title: ng says /ng/
parentNote: The last few days were blends — two letters, two sounds, said in a hurry: sw, fl, fr. Today is the other kind of pair. In king, sing and long the n and the g do not take turns; together they make one single new sound, made right at the back of the mouth, the hum you end a yawn with. The mistake is almost always saying the letters separately, so "sing" comes out "sinn-guh" and "long" gets a hard g on the end. Say the whole word yourself first and let them hear that it stops with a hum, not a pop. Today also brings the first two-syllable words in a while — digging, standing — so cover the second half with a finger, read the first half, then slide your finger away.

activities.mouthCue: The back of your tongue lifts up and blocks your mouth, so the hum goes out of your nose instead.
activities.prompt: The last few days were two letters in a hurry. These two are not in a hurry — together they make one brand new sound.
Three hums. This one is made right at the back of your mouth.
One of these is two sounds in a hurry. The other is one sound on its own. Find the one sound.
Three sounds, not four. Keep ng together — it is one sound.
Only the first sound has changed. Keep the ending exactly the same.
Same ending, with a round mouth in the middle.
A long one. Read dig, then add ing on the back: dig — ing.
The longest one. Read stand, then add ing on the back: stand — ing.
One of these stops with a hum and one stops with a pop.
Same again. Is the ending one sound or two?
Same start, same ending. Listen hard to the middle.

activities.title: The long song
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: The king sang a long song in the shop.
The song did not stop and the cat ran off.
The dog sat and did sing back at the king.
The king did stop and did grin at the dog.
The cat ran back in and sat on the king!
